title: Symmetric bimodules come from module objects
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a braided monoidal category and $\mathcal R$ a commutative monoid
object. Let $P$ be a symmetric $\mathcal R$-$\mathcal R$-bimodule in the sense of
[lem-sfb-modobj-symmetric-bimodules], and let $M$ be the $\mathcal R$-module object
obtained by forgetting the right action of $P$. Then the identity of the underlying
object is an isomorphism of bimodules from the bimodule attached to $M$ in
[lem-sfb-modobj-symmetric-bimodules] to $P$. Hence every symmetric bimodule is
isomorphic to the bimodule attached to a module object.

proof.text: Write $Q$ for the bimodule attached to the underlying left module $M$ of $P$. By [lem-sfb-modobj-symmetric-bimodules], $Q$ has underlying object $P$, left action $\gamma_P$, and right action $\gamma_P\circ\beta_{P,\mathcal R}=\rho_P$, the last equality being the symmetry hypothesis on $P$. Thus $Q$ and $P$ have identical action maps. In either direction the underlying identity $1_P$ is a bimodule morphism: its left compatibility equation reduces to $\gamma_P=\gamma_P$ and its right compatibility equation to $\rho_P=\rho_P$, since tensoring preserves identities. Taking these two identity maps as forward and inverse maps, both composites are the identity on the underlying object, hence the identity bimodule morphisms. This gives the asserted isomorphism $Q\cong P$.
